new_findings_today.title: REGRESSION: Explore map renders zero markers (511 → 0) — map mounts, data loads, marker layer never attaches
new_findings_today.detail: On /en/explore Map toggle: Leaflet mounts (1 container, 18 tiles, window.L object, OSM/CARTO attribution, score legend) and the label still reads '511 markers · colored by score' — but the overlay pane has 0 children (no SVG, no canvas), marker pane 0, across 3 probes spanning ~25 s including after a zoom interaction. Yesterday (2026-06-07) the same probe found 511 score-colored circleMarker paths, visually confirmed. The label knowing the count proves the data fetch succeeds; the circleMarker layer silently fails to attach. No console errors. Coincides with the new deployment dpl_7LxrP7U8A6RdNJLkRxfhoCfLYznq. Destination-page Leaflet maps are unaffected (betla, vishnuprayag each render their 1 overlay marker), so this is specific to the explore marker-layer code path, not Leaflet-wide. Also observed (pre-existing?): initial map viewport centers on the Afghanistan/Pakistan region with India in the lower half — check fitBounds while fixing markers.
new_findings_today.evidence: section-K-map.csv rows explore-map-toggle + explore-map-zoom-reprobe; pane census map-pane:8, tile-pane:1, overlay-pane:0, marker-pane:0; screenshots ss_9770b8m6b, ss_63885crpq (markerless India map with legend promising colored dots); compare 2026-06-07 findings INFO-2026-06-07-003 (511 paths).
new_findings_today.recommendation: Triage against the new deploy's diff to explore-map.tsx / explore-with-map.tsx (or shared marker-layer util). Suspects: circleMarker layer-group add removed/conditioned out, an early-return on a renamed prop, or pane/renderer option change (svg renderer no longer instantiated). The 'Map' toggle is the flagship discovery surface — recommend same-day fix or rollback.
new_findings_today.verified_followup: VERIFIED 2026-06-08 ~02:40 UTC (live Playwright, warm load): explore Map toggle renders all 511 markers as SVG <path> in the overlay pane, sampled every 500ms from t=0 to t=6s — consistently 511, 0 console errors. So markers are NOT broken on warm loads. ROOT CAUSE (code-confirmed, not the deploy diff — explore-map.tsx unchanged since 2026-06-05): a render race between the two useEffects in explore-map.tsx. Effect 1 sets mapInstanceRef only after `import('leaflet')` resolves; Effect 2 (markers) fires a SINGLE 500ms setTimeout retry and gives up permanently if the map isn't ready by then. mapDestinations (parent useMemo) is stable unless a filter changes, so Effect 2 never re-runs to rescue. When the Leaflet chunk is COLD (uncached) the import exceeds 500ms — exactly the state right after a deploy cache-bust, which is when the harness probes — so markers never attach while the parent's count label still reads 511 (separate state). The harness probe was CORRECT (overlay_svg_paths=0 was real at that cold moment); this is a genuine intermittent bug, not a harness false positive, but it self-recovers on any filter change and is invisible on warm loads. FIX: PR fix/explore-map-marker-race-2026-06-08 adds a `mapReady` state set when the map instance exists and adds it to the marker effect deps, so markers attach as soon as the import resolves regardless of timing. NOT a rollback case.

new_findings_today.verified_followup: VERIFIED 2026-06-08 ~02:43 UTC (live Playwright): #418 reproduces on /en/destination/betla and /en/explore (same rX/iu/sd stack, deploy dpl_7LxrP7U8). REAL. BUT: (1) the deploy did NOT touch the root layout or any of its client components (CompareProvider/ScrollToTop/PageTransition/MobileTabBar/GA4RouteTracker/MotionProvider/StickyCTA/PWAInstallPrompt/OfflineIndicator/SaveListEmailPrompt/PersonalisationQuiz) — so this is NOT a deploy regression and the 'escalation' narrative is likely sampling noise on a pre-existing intermittent error. (2) Two consecutive server renders of betla are BYTE-IDENTICAL (82,204 chars, zero divergence) — so the SSR is deterministic and the mismatch is CLIENT-SIDE: a layout client component renders different markup on first client paint than the server (classic browser-state-read-during-render: localStorage/matchMedia/window/navigator in a render body or useState initializer). The masthead-month theory is ruled out (deterministic SSR; masthead lives on editorial pages, not betla). NEXT STEP unchanged: non-minified `next dev` repro on /en/destination/betla, then audit the listed layout client components for browser-state reads outside useEffect. Tracked as a proportionate follow-up — recoverable, no user-visible breakage, not blocking.

new_findings_today.title: Harness incident prevented, worth keeping: stale root-owned /tmp/_body from yesterday's run silently poisoned today's first probes
new_findings_today.detail: /tmp persists across daily sandbox sessions but file ownership doesn't (yesterday's files are nobody:nogroup, unwritable). probe.py wrote curl bodies to the fixed path /tmp/_body; today curl exited rc=23 (write error) while -w still emitted '200', so the probe read YESTERDAY'S 712KB HTML as today's sitemap and the sample draw crashed (which is how it was caught — a quieter section could have produced wrong-but-plausible data). Fixed in today's probe.py: per-run temp paths (/tmp/_body_20260608) + hard-fail on any curl nonzero exit. Related minor gotcha documented in PWA-2026-05-05: sw-version regex first-match reads the in-file version changelog (v32), not CACHE_VERSION (v51).
new_findings_today.evidence: ls -la /tmp/_body → nobody:nogroup Jun 7 02:15; probe.py diff in qa/findings/2026-06-08/.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Keep per-run temp paths + rc!=0 hard-fail in future probe.py copies (today's file is the template). Never trust -w output without checking curl's exit code.
